item.title: Nvidia, S&P 500 Face Risks From US China AI Chip Curbs
item.description: Can the US crush China’s artificial-intelligence dreams without hurting itself? This is the question politicians in Washington must ask themselves. The blow to China is severe. The US has closed a long-standing loophole that allowed Chinese AI labs remote access to advanced American chips sold overseas. item.dc:creator: Shuli Ren

item.title: AI Is Sucking Turbines From Other Industries
item.description: What connects a $3.7 billion writedown at SoftBank; the second-biggest takeover in General Electric’s history; the revival of a 250-year-old British industrial company; delays to container ships and a promised supersonic airliner; construction problems at power stations on two continents; and soaring natural gas pipeline costs?The answer is the artificial intelligence boom — and its insatiable hunger for energy.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: Japan’s Quantum Dawn Is Here. Now Comes the Hard Part
item.description: It wasn’t immediately clear whether I was stepping into the past or the future when I got a peek at a computer that took up an entire room. But, as in quantum mechanics, it felt as if two possibilities could exist at once.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Thorbecke

item.title: COP31: Climate Summit Fails When It Can’t Even Say ‘Fossil Fuels’
item.description: The 31st United Nations climate conference was expected to be a fairly dull affair, focusing on “implementation.” Instead, it will be one for the history books as a dramatic final showdown failed to result in an agreement for only the second time since climate COPs began in 1995.
item.dc:creator: Lara Williams

item.title: Newsom’s AI Populism Is a Bid to Stay Relevant
item.description: Now that the midterm elections are over, attention among those who just can’t get enough of politics has inevitably shifted to the 2028 presidential race. Who’s running? Who’s not running? These questions will be answered in the coming weeks and months.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: Rubio 2028 Rumors: Can He Restore the Republican Party?
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio is suddenly everywhere, all at once. At the president’s side for his meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Briefing reporters on cyber glitches that have, in theory, nothing to do with his day job as secretary of state. All over the headlines as a new round of polls shows more Republicans want him to succeed President Donald Trump than want Vice President JD Vance or other Republicans to do so.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: Electric? Luxury? Driverless? Your Car’s Falling Apart Anyway
item.description: The entire auto industry may be in a funk, but at least gasoline prices are down.
item.dc:creator: Toby Harshaw
